90	> ### Design direction for re-proposal
91	>
92	> The following decisions are recorded here so the future ADR-013
93	> re-proposer can adopt them without re-deriving the rationale. They
94	> are constraints, not interface contract — CONTRACT-004 and ADR-014
95	> remain unaffected and transport-agnostic.
96	>
97	> 1. **Transport**: in-process PTY via the existing `internal/pty/`
98	>    library, with hooks registered via `--settings '<inline-json>'`
99	>    (Anthropic-published extension point). The `--settings` flag is
100	>    explicitly distinguished from the previously-forbidden batch flags
101	>    (`--print`, `-p`, `--output-format`, `--stream-json`, `--effort`,
102	>    `--model`, `--permission-mode`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`)
103	>    because it configures end-user-facing behavior the way a user's
104	>    `~/.claude/settings.json` would, not an automation/batch mode. The
105	>    batch-flag prohibition stands; the `--settings` carve-out is
106	>    additive.
107	>
108	> 2. **Output parsing**: read the JSONL transcript whose path is
109	>    delivered in the `Stop` hook payload. Do not parse rendered TUI
110	>    output. `internal/pty/terminal` (vt10x) is not required for
111	>    Execute; the PTY layer is reduced to "enough to keep Ink happy at
112	>    startup" — a small responder for DA1 / DA2 / DSR / XTVERSION /
113	>    window-size probes. A reusable startup-probe responder belongs in
114	>    `internal/pty/` so the quota probe path can consume it too.
115	>
116	> 3. **Streaming progress events**: use `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse`
117	>    hooks (or whichever Claude Code hooks are documented for tool-call
118	>    boundaries at re-proposal time) to emit `tool_call` / `tool_result`
119	>    events during the turn. claude-p is batch (only `Stop`); Fizeau's
120	>    CONTRACT-004 requires intermediate `ProgressEvents` so this hook
121	>    set is load-bearing.
122	>
123	> 4. **Session lifetime**: **pooled long-lived sessions with `/clear`
124	>    between turns, lifetime bounded by the fiz process**. Rationale:
125	>    Ink + auth startup is the expensive part (~50–200 ms per claude-p's
126	>    measurements); amortizing it across the many Execute calls within
127	>    a single fiz invocation is worth the pool-management cost.
128	>    `/clear` resets conversation state without dropping the warm
129	>    session. The pool dies when fiz dies — no PID files, no daemon, no
130	>    cross-invocation persistence.
131	>
132	>    Pool key default: **per `(harness, workdir)`**. Claude sessions
133	>    are bound to a working directory at startup; switching workdirs in
134	>    an existing session is not supported by `claude`. Per-(harness)
135	>    only would force serialization across all workdirs;
136	>    per-(harness, workdir, model) is overkill — model selection is
137	>    cheap enough to run via `/model` post-`/clear`.
138	>
139	>    Pool depth default: **1 per key**. Adequate for serial agent
140	>    loops, which is the standalone CLI's usage. Service-mode
141	>    concurrency can raise this with no contract change.
142	>
143	>    Pool placement: the pool lives at package scope (a singleton in
144	>    `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/`) or at service scope (a
145	>    constructor-injected dependency on the Runner), **not as a field
146	>    on the Runner struct**. Two `&claudetui.Runner{}` instances must
147	>    share the pool, otherwise the dispatcher's "construct a fresh
148	>    Runner per Execute" pattern defeats the amortization. CONTRACT-004
149	>    invariant #6 forbids mutable quota/account state on the Runner
150	>    but does not forbid shared transport state behind a singleton;
151	>    this is the right escape valve.
152	>
153	> 5. **Empirical `/clear` semantics gate** (pre-implementation): verify
154	>    against the installed Claude Code that `/clear`:
155	>    - resets conversation history (the point of the command);
156	>    - does NOT reset model selection (otherwise per-turn `/model` is
157	>      required, lengthening the per-turn ritual);
158	>    - does NOT reset permission mode;
159	>    - does NOT close the auth/session token;
160	>    - starts a new transcript file at a path observable from the
161	>      next turn's `Stop` hook payload.
162	>
163	>    If any of those don't hold, the per-turn ritual lengthens but
164	>    the pool model is still worthwhile. If `/clear` doesn't exist or
165	>    is unstable in the installed version, fall back to per-Execute
166	>    sessions (claude-p model) and accept the cold-start cost.
167	>
168	> 6. **Orphan reaper**: fiz crashes leave pooled `claude` processes
169	>    orphaned. A startup reaper analogous to the existing
170	>    `service_stale_harness_reaper*.go` kills `claude` processes whose
171	>    parent fiz PID is gone, before the new fiz instance constructs
172	>    its pool. No persistent state across fiz invocations — the
173	>    reaper inspects live process state only.
174	>
175	> 7. **Hook conflict handling**: a user's existing
176	>    `~/.claude/settings.json` may declare its own `SessionStart` /
177	>    `Stop` / `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` hooks. The `--settings
178	>    '<inline-json>'` mechanism's merge semantics (replace vs. layer)
179	>    are unspecified in claude-p's README and need explicit
180	>    verification before claude-tui can ship. If hooks are
181	>    replace-not-merge, Fizeau must compose with whatever the operator
182	>    already has, not stomp it.
183	>
184	> 8. **Subscription billing observation**: still required as a
185	>    promotion gate per ADR-014. Neither claude-p nor shannon claims
186	>    subscription billing; both route through the same `claude`
187	>    binary and inherit whatever billing classification that binary's
188	>    request paths produce. The re-proposal must include an empirical
189	>    measurement showing PTY+hooks-driven Claude moves the `/usage`

197	## Context
198	
199	The current `claude` harness (`internal/harnesses/claude/runner.go`) drives the
200	Claude CLI through `claude --print -p --output-format stream-json` (with a
201	legacy `--output-format json` fallback) via `os/exec`. That subprocess path
202	covers normal prompt execution today, but it is a different transport from the
203	direct PTY path Fizeau already uses for `/usage` quota probing
204	(`internal/harnesses/claude/quota_pty.go` over `internal/harnesses/ptyquota`,
205	`internal/pty/session`, `internal/pty/terminal`).
206	
207	**The driver for forking is Anthropic subscription pricing.** Claude Pro/Max
208	subscription capacity is billed against an account quota that is exposed
209	through the interactive Claude CLI surface (TUI + `/usage`). The Anthropic
210	API, including request paths a `claude --print` invocation may resolve
211	against, is metered separately at per-token API pricing. Routing prompt
212	execution through the interactive TUI is how Fizeau accesses subsidized
213	subscription capacity (ADR-011 cost-based routing already assumes this is
214	possible). The existing `claude --print` transport cannot be relied on to
215	keep landing on subscription capacity as Anthropic evolves the boundary; the
216	TUI surface is the durable, documented entry point for subscription quota.
217	
218	This is not about anti-automation fingerprinting or impersonating a human as
219	a security goal. It is about using the subscription product the way it is
220	priced, which means: drive the TUI, do not pass batch-API-shaped flags, and
221	do not introduce Fizeau-side signals (env vars, argv markers) that change
222	billing classification or invite policy enforcement against automated batch
223	use.
224	
225	ADR-002 already commits Fizeau to direct PTY ownership and bans tmux from the
226	core path. ADR-004 caps build vs. buy for the PTY library boundary. ADR-011
227	treats subsidized Claude/Codex quota as a routing-preferred capacity pool.
228	None of those ADRs specify *how* normal prompt execution should adopt PTY
229	without breaking the existing `claude` evidence base (cassettes, runner
230	tests, capability baseline rows, auto-routing eligibility).
231	
232	## Decision
233	
234	Fizeau will add a **new, separate primary harness identity `claude-tui`** that
235	implements the existing `harnesses.Harness` interface
236	(`internal/harnesses/types.go`, `Info`/`HealthCheck`/`Execute`) and runs the
237	Claude CLI exclusively through the direct PTY transport. `claude-tui` is a
238	fork — a sibling package alongside `internal/harnesses/claude/` — not a
239	mode, flag, or conditional branch in the existing runner.
240	
241	The existing `claude` harness keeps its current implementation, capability
242	evidence, and auto-routing eligibility unchanged. Both harnesses coexist
243	indefinitely; capability and routing decisions are tracked per-identity.
244	
245	`claude-tui` is the identity through which subscription-billed Claude
246	capacity is routed once it earns auto-routing eligibility. Until then, the
247	existing `claude` harness continues to serve routed Claude traffic.
248	
249	**Key Points**: separate package + registry identity | PTY only, no batch
250	flags, no Fizeau-side identification env/argv | both `claude` and
251	`claude-tui` are primary harnesses with independent baseline rows | both
252	implement the same `harnesses.Harness` interface.
253	
254	## Harness Interface (Normative)
255	
256	The new identity implements the existing, unchanged interface defined in
257	`internal/harnesses/types.go`:
258	
259	```go
260	type Harness interface {
261	    // Info returns identity + capability metadata for this harness.
262	    Info() HarnessInfo
263	
264	    // HealthCheck triggers a fresh probe (binary present, auth ok, etc.)
265	    // and returns nil if the harness is ready to execute.
266	    HealthCheck(ctx context.Context) error
267	
268	    // Execute runs one resolved request. Events stream on the returned
269	    // channel; a single final event closes the stream. The first error
270	    // return is reserved for setup failures (binary missing, etc.) — once
271	    // the channel is returned, all per-run failures are reported via a
272	    // final event with Status != "success".
273	    Execute(ctx context.Context, req ExecuteRequest) (<-chan Event, error)
274	}
275	```
276	
277	`HarnessInfo`, `ExecuteRequest`, `Event`, `FinalData`, `FinalUsage`,
278	`RoutingActual`, `ReasoningActual`, and the `EventType` closed union are
279	defined in the same file and are not extended by this ADR. CONTRACT-003 is
280	the public-surface contract that those internal shapes reflect; this ADR
281	adds no new event types, no new request fields, and no new metadata keys.
282	
283	`claude-tui` therefore differs from `claude` only in:
284	
285	- transport mechanism (PTY vs. `os/exec` batch),
286	- registry config (`HarnessConfig`) entry name, binary invocation, and
287	  baseline flags,
288	- `HarnessInfo.Name` returned by `Info()`,
289	- internal package layout and tests,
290	
291	not in interface, event shapes, or request semantics. A caller routing
292	through `harnesses.Harness` cannot tell the two apart except by the
293	`HarnessInfo.Name` it returns.
294	
295	A separate harness identity (rather than a `Transport` mode on a single
296	`HarnessConfig`) is required because:
297	
298	- `HarnessInfo.Name` is the key the capability matrix, routing layer, and
299	  evidence store use to attribute rows. Collapsing two transports into one
300	  name makes evidence ambiguous.
301	- `HarnessConfig` carries `BaseArgs`, `PermissionArgs`, `ModelFlag`,
302	  `ReasoningFlag`, and `TUIQuotaCommand` fields that have transport-specific
303	  meaning. A PTY harness uses none of `BaseArgs`/`ModelFlag`/`ReasoningFlag`
304	  and uses `TUIQuotaCommand`-shaped flows for routine model/reasoning
305	  selection, not just for quota. Two configs is cheaper than a polymorphic
306	  one.
307	- `AutoRoutingEligible` is a per-row decision in the primary baseline. It
308	  must be expressible independently for the PTY transport, which has no
309	  live cassette evidence at introduction.

311	## Scope
312

328	### Out of Scope

340	## Invocation Constraints
341	
342	These constraints derive from the subscription-pricing goal: invocation must
343	not look like batch-API automation, and Fizeau must not introduce side
344	channels that could be used to reclassify the request.
345	
346	`claude-tui` **must not**:
347	
348	- Pass any flag that signals batch/automation intent or selects a non-TUI
349	  output format: `--print`, `-p`, `--output-format`, `--stream-json`,
350	  `--effort`, `--model`, `--permission-mode`,
351	  `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, or any future Anthropic flag in the same
352	  family. Where a TUI affordance for the same setting exists (e.g. a `/model`
353	  selector), use that affordance via PTY input bytes. Where no TUI affordance
354	  exists, the capability is `gap` for `claude-tui` until one does — do not
355	  silently fall back to a CLI flag.
356	- Introduce Fizeau-side environment variables that identify the caller as an
357	  agent: no `CLAUDE_*`, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `*_AGENT*`, `*_AUTOMATED*`, or similar
358	  Fizeau-introduced names on this path. Pre-existing variables already set
359	  in the operator's environment are passed through unchanged via the
360	  documented allowlist below.
361	- Send single-keystroke input bursts faster than the configured inter-key
362	  delay band (default 25–75ms per logical key). Pasted prompts go through
363	  bracketed paste and may arrive as one burst; that matches real paste
364	  behavior and is allowed.
365	
366	`claude-tui` **may**:
367	
368	- Use the bracketed-paste sequence to deliver a multi-line prompt in one
369	  event. Bracketed paste is the documented terminal mechanism for paste
370	  input and is what a real paste produces.
371	- Read raw PTY bytes, derive frames through `internal/pty/terminal`, and
372	  emit Fizeau service events from them. Service-event emission is internal
373	  to Fizeau and is not visible to the Claude binary.
374	- Cancel a turn with the key combination the TUI documents for cancellation
375	  (Esc by default; Ctrl-C as a fallback that exits the session, in which
376	  case `claude-tui` restarts a session for the next request).
377	- Reuse the existing `internal/pty/cassette` recorder and
378	  `internal/ptytest` assertion framework with no modifications beyond a new
379	  harness name and scenario fixtures.

381	### Environment Allowlist
382	
383	The PTY session is started with the following environment, exactly:
384	
385	- Pass-through from the operator environment: `HOME`, `PATH`, `USER`,

395	
396	Anything else is dropped. The cassette manifest's `env_allowlist` records
397	the exact set used per recording so future spec amendments can be reviewed
398	against captured evidence.
399	
400	## Module Boundaries
401	
402	Per ADR-002, no package below `internal/pty` may import
403	`internal/harnesses`. `claude-tui` honors that boundary:
404	
405	| Layer | Path | Owns |
406	|-------|------|------|
407	| Runner | `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/runner.go` | Implements `harnesses.Harness` (`Info`, `HealthCheck`, `Execute`); owns event emission, prompt delivery, slash-command drivers for model/reasoning/permission selection, cancellation, timeout enforcement, idle timeout, request-metadata stamping. |
408	| TUI parser | `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/stream.go` | Frame-derived parsing of the Claude TUI: prompt echo recognition, assistant message extraction, tool-call/tool-result framing, usage extraction from `/cost` or equivalent TUI surfaces, final-event derivation. Must not import `internal/harnesses/claude`. |
409	| Model/reasoning discovery | `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/model_discovery.go` | TUI-driven model and reasoning enumeration. Persists results into `internal/harnesses.ModelDiscoveryCache` keyed by `claude-tui` so it does not collide with `claude` evidence. |
410	| Shared neutral helpers | `internal/harnesses/anthropic/` | `IsClaudeQuotaExhaustedMessage`, `MarkClaudeQuotaExhaustedFromMessage`, account-info shapes, model-name normalization. Consumed by both `claude` and `claude-tui`. Has no dependency on either harness package. |
411	| Quota reuse | (consumed, not re-implemented) | `claude-tui` reads `ClaudeQuotaSnapshot` from the existing durable cache. It does not own a parallel quota probe. |
412	| Cassettes/tests | `internal/harnesses/claude-tui/testdata/` and `internal/ptytest` scenarios | Live record cassettes per capability row; replay-only tests for default CI. |
413	
414	The `claude-tui` runner must not import `internal/harnesses/claude`, and the
415	`claude` runner must not import `internal/harnesses/claude-tui`. The
416	`internal/harnesses/anthropic` neutral package is the only allowed sharing
417	seam.
418	
419	## Capability Baseline Impact
420	
421	`primary-harness-capability-baseline.md` adds a fifth row, `claude-tui`. At
422	introduction every row is `gap` until live PTY record-mode evidence exists,
423	mirroring how `claude` quota status was originally gated. The
424	`AutoRoutingEligible` flag stays `false` for `claude-tui` until promotion.
425	
426	Known gaps at introduction with documented blockers (not optimistic
427	"pending evidence"):
428	
429	| Row | Status | Known blocker |
430	|-----|--------|---------------|
431	| PermissionModes (`unrestricted`) | `gap`, no TUI affordance known | The `claude --print` path uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; no equivalent TUI affordance is documented today. Until a `/permissions bypass` or similar surface ships, `claude-tui` exposes only `safe` and `supervised`. |
432	| SetReasoning | `gap`, no TUI affordance known | The `claude --print` path uses `--effort`; no documented Claude TUI slash command sets per-turn reasoning. Until one ships, `claude-tui` does not set reasoning and treats requested non-default values as a routing rejection. |
433	| All other rows | `gap` until live cassette evidence | Standard ADR-002 promotion path. |
434	
435	Once any `claude-tui` capability has accepted live cassette evidence, the
436	row becomes `pass` independently of `claude`. A `pass` on `claude` does not
437	imply `pass` on `claude-tui`, and vice versa.
438	
439	`harness-golden-integration.md` extends the cassette scenario list to
440	include `claude-tui` authenticated record mode plus replay cassettes for
441	each capability row that has a TUI affordance.
442	
443	## Performance and Cost Acknowledgement
444	
445	The fork is not free:
446	
447	- **Parsing cost**: Frame derivation through `internal/pty/terminal`
448	  (vt10x-backed) on every spinner/render update is meaningfully more
449	  expensive than parsing `stream-json` JSONL lines. For long turns with
450	  many redraws the CPU and wall-clock cost is noticeable. The benchmark
451	  suite (`scripts/benchmark/`) must include a `claude-tui` lane so this
452	  cost is measured before promotion to auto-routing.
453	- **Per-turn latency**: Inter-key delays for menu navigation add a fixed
454	  overhead (commonly a few hundred ms total) per turn that selects
455	  model/reasoning. Bracketed-paste prompts do not add latency.
456	- **Code duplication**: Two runners, two parsers, two discovery paths, two
457	  cassette suites. Estimated 1500–2500 LOC of additional code carried
458	  indefinitely (the existing `claude` package is ~3.5k LOC across
459	  runner/stream/quota; `claude-tui` will be smaller because it skips the
460	  stream-json fallback path and the `--print` argument builder). Review
461	  burden is the larger long-term cost.
462	
463	These costs are accepted because subscription pricing is the load-bearing
464	economic constraint for primary-routing Claude capacity (ADR-011). If
465	`claude --print` ever lands on subscription capacity reliably and durably
466	without TUI-driven traffic, this ADR is open to revision.
467	
468	## Alternatives
469	
470	| Option | Pros | Cons | Evaluation |
471	|--------|------|------|------------|
472	| **Fork as `claude-tui` (selected)** | Two implementations evolve independently; capability evidence is unambiguous per identity; honors ADR-002 PTY-first design; allows `claude` to keep shipping while PTY work matures; lets the routing layer treat subscription-billed and API-billed Claude as distinct supply pools. | One-time duplication of runner scaffolding; risk of drift in shared parsing helpers (mitigated by extracting them to `internal/harnesses/anthropic`). | **Selected**: matches the subscription-pricing driver, matches ADR-002's library-first boundary, and avoids hidden conditional branches in the hot path. |
473	| Add a `Transport` mode to existing `claude.Runner` | No new package; smaller code footprint at first. | Conditionals in every hot path (Execute, stream parsing, model discovery, error classification); capability evidence becomes ambiguous because the harness identity collapses two transports into one row; auto-routing eligibility decisions cannot be expressed cleanly; `HarnessConfig` fields like `BaseArgs` and `ModelFlag` have no meaning for half the configurations of a single name. | Rejected: explicitly the failure mode the user called out. |
474	| Replace `claude` with PTY-only implementation now | Single canonical path. | Throws away existing `--print` cassettes, runner tests, and quota/auto-routing evidence before PTY parity is proven; high risk of regressing primary subscription capacity. | Rejected: parity is unproven; coexistence is cheaper and safer. |
475	| Drive PTY through tmux | Reuses well-trodden multiplexer patterns. | ADR-002 already rejected this for the core path; would inherit global tmux server state and weaken cassette determinism. | Rejected by ADR-002. |
476	| Build a generic "TUI harness" abstraction now, parameterized per CLI | One library covers Claude, Codex, Gemini. | Premature: only Claude needs this today; the right shape is unclear until at least two consumers exist; would slow `claude-tui` shipping. | Rejected for now; revisit if a second consumer emerges. |
477	
478	## Consequences
479	
480	| Type | Impact |
481	|------|--------|
482	| Positive | Subscription-billed Claude capacity is accessible through a stable, documented TUI surface. |
483	| Positive | Capability evidence stays unambiguous: each harness identity owns its own baseline row. |
484	| Positive | The existing `claude` harness, its tests, and its operator-visible behavior are unaffected during the rollout. |
485	| Positive | The routing layer can treat subscription-billed (`claude-tui`) and API-billed (`claude`) Claude as distinct supply pools with distinct cost classes. |
486	| Negative | The codebase carries two Claude runners until a future retirement ADR. Reviewers must keep them honestly separate. |
487	| Negative | Frame-derived parsing has a real CPU cost relative to stream-json parsing. Benchmark lane required before auto-routing promotion. |
488	| Negative | Live record-mode cassettes for `claude-tui` need authentication and quota windows; CI footprint grows on opt-in record runs. |
489	| Negative | Some capability rows (`unrestricted` permissions, per-turn reasoning) are blocked indefinitely until Anthropic ships TUI affordances. |
490	| Neutral | Quota evidence is shared across both Claude identities because Anthropic accounts limit per account, not per Fizeau-side transport — under the named single-account assumption. |
491	
492	## Risks
493	
494	| Risk | Prob | Impact | Mitigation |
495	|------|------|--------|------------|
496	| Shared parsing helpers drift between `claude` and `claude-tui` | M | M | Extract genuinely shared helpers into `internal/harnesses/anthropic` before consuming from both runners; cover with helper-level tests; lint rule blocks cross-imports. |
497	| TUI surface changes break the parser between Claude CLI releases | H | M | Cassette manifests pin binary version; replay tests pin manifest IDs and content digests (ADR-002 contract); a TUI surface change that breaks parsing surfaces as a capability `gap` in the matrix, not as silent execution failures. |
498	| Operators conflate `claude` and `claude-tui` in routing config | M | L | Routing surface treats the two identities as fully distinct (already true via primary baseline rows); error messages from the routing layer name the exact identity that was selected. |
499	| Single-account quota assumption fails for multi-account operators | L | M | Cache key gains an account dimension in a follow-up spec when the first multi-account user report lands; until then, document the assumption in the routing snapshot. |
500	| Anthropic changes the boundary between subscription and API billing such that PTY no longer guarantees subscription routing | L | H | The ADR is open to revision; the fork's coexistence design means `claude` remains available as the API-billed path with no code change required to fall back. |

# Billing Observation: claude-tui PTY+Hooks Mode

**Date**: 2026-05-27  
**Purpose**: Pre-registered methodology for empirical capture of subscription-mode billing classification for Claude TUI invocations via PTY+hooks transport.  
**Status**: METHODOLOGY — Document defines experiment method; measurement placeholders below are filled by sibling beads.

## Measurement Methodology

This section pre-registers the method for capturing empirical billing evidence per ADR-013 constraint #8.

### Model

**Recommended Model**: `claude-sonnet-4-6`  
**Rationale**: Widely deployed, stable TUI support across versions; fallback to `claude-opus-4-7` if sonnet unavailable at measurement time.  
**Selection**: Single model across all measurement runs to ensure billing classification is consistent per model version.

### Prompt

**Prompt Characteristics**:
- **Type**: Non-trivial coding task
- **Expected Output Tokens**: 500–2000 range (medium-length generated code + explanation)
- **Justification**: Sufficient complexity to generate meaningful subscription-window activity while remaining deterministic across runs; avoids trivial arithmetic prompts that may produce <100 tokens and risk quota-accounting edge cases

### Single-Account Constraint

**Constraint**: No concurrent Claude CLI invocations from the same account during the measurement window.

### /usage Refresh-Delay Safety Margin

**Documented Refresh Delay**: `/usage` snapshots in the Claude TUI reflect quota state with a post-completion delay.

**Safety Margin Applied**: ≥60 seconds post-completion  
**Rationale**: Empirical observation (from prior measurements) shows quota deltas are observable within 60–90s; using 60s as the floor ensures AFTER snapshots see the message-count delta.

**Measurement Protocol**:
1. Record completion timestamp (wall-clock, UTC)
2. Wait ≥60 seconds
3. Run `/usage` command and capture the snapshot
4. Record snapshot timestamp (wall-clock, UTC)
5. Verify delta: completion-time ≤ snapshot-time (confirm refresh was honored)

## Verdict Decision Rule

This section defines the classification verdicts based on observed /usage delta patterns.

### Three-Outcome Classification

**Input**: BEFORE snapshot, AFTER snapshot (both captured per refresh-delay protocol), delta computed across the pair.

**Outcomes**:

| Verdict | Criteria | Evidence |

| **subscription-confirmed** | (1) BEFORE and AFTER both report `Billing Mode: subscription`; (2) Weekly usage delta is exactly +1 message; (3) AFTER timestamp ≥ completion-time + 60s; (4) No API-metering indicators in either snapshot. | Billing classification changed from subscription to subscription; quota window incremented; refresh-delay respected. |

| **subscription-ambiguous** | (1) BEFORE or AFTER snapshots are malformed/unreadable; OR (2) `/usage` command failed during measurement; OR (3) Unclear or missing billing-classification field in snapshot; OR (4) Single-account attestation not provided. | Insufficient evidence to classify; measurement must be re-run with corrected protocol. |

### Verdict Aggregation

**Per-Run Verdict**: Each of the 3 PTY+hooks runs and each of the 3 `--print` mode runs receives a single verdict (subscription-confirmed, subscription-rejected, or subscription-ambiguous).

**Overall Verdict** (across all 6 runs):
- **Billing evidence accepted** if 5 or 6 runs report subscription-confirmed
- **Billing evidence rejected** if any run reports subscription-rejected
- **Billing evidence inconclusive** if ≥1 run reports subscription-ambiguous and no subscription-rejected runs

- If overall verdict is **accepted**: ADR-013 constraint #8 is fulfilled; promotion decision for `claude-tui` auto-routing eligibility can proceed
